title: crossentropy
summary: Compute cross-entropy loss for host numeric predictions and targets.
description: `crossentropy(Y,T)` computes cross-entropy over same-sized host numeric arrays or `dlarray` compatibility objects.
behaviors: Inputs must be finite, non-empty numeric arrays or host-backed `dlarray` objects with the same number of elements.
Predictions are clipped to a small open interval before taking logarithms; targets must be probabilities in the range [0, 1].
The third positional argument or `Weights` name-value option may provide scalar, prediction-sized, channel-sized, or observation-sized weights.
`DataFormat` and `WeightsFormat` validate RunMat's supported deep-learning labels `S`, `C`, `B`, `T`, and `U`; `WeightsFormat` maps weight dimensions to prediction dimensions by label.
`Reduction` supports `sum` and `none`; unreduced output preserves the prediction shape.
`Mask` must be a full-size logical or binary numeric array.
Host `dlarray` inputs return host `dlarray` compatibility outputs; reduced scalar losses and unreduced loss arrays are returned as unformatted `dlarray` objects.
Datastore/category target expansion, automatic differentiation, and provider-resident execution remain future work.

examples.output: Weighted scalar loss normalized by batch size.

example.input: loss = crossentropy(Y, T, weights, Name, Value)

gpu_residency: `crossentropy` runs on host tensors or host-backed `dlarray` objects in this slice. Provider kernels and GPU residency preservation are tracked by the queued GPU fast-path audit.
